Answer: A
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 1b) shows a radiolucent mass in the anterior superior chest with obtuse angles to the chest wall, which is characteristic of an extrapleural fat collection (such as a lipoma or prominent extrapleural fat) rather than an intrapulmonary lesion. This morphology and anterior location help differentiate it from other fat-containing lesions like hernias or intrathoracic masses.
